questions.stem: Which assemblage is the minimum MQSA definition of a mammography unit?

choices.text: Generator, control, tube housing, beam-limiting device, and supporting structures
choices.rationale: Correct. These are the minimum components in § 900.2(dd).

choices.text: Only a digital detector and a compression paddle
choices.rationale: A detector and paddle alone omit required components.

choices.text: Any general radiographic room plus a mammography attachment
choices.rationale: General-purpose systems with attachments are prohibited.

choices.text: A mobile coach without an x-ray control
choices.rationale: An x-ray control is required.

questions.explanation: MQSA defines a mammography unit as including at least generator, control, tube housing assembly, beam-limiting device, and supports.

variants.simpler: Five parts minimum: make x-rays, control them, house the tube, limit the beam, and support them.
variants.example: If a schematic omits the beam-limiting device, it is incomplete.

questions.stem: A clinic proposes using a general radiographic unit fitted with a mammography compression attachment. Under MQSA, this is:

choices.rationale: Surveys do not legalize prohibited equipment.

choices.text: Allowed for screening but not diagnostic exams
choices.rationale: The prohibition is not limited by exam type.

choices.text: Prohibited; mammography must use equipment specifically designed for mammography
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches the cited source for this item.

choices.text: Allowed only with DBT software enabled
choices.rationale: Software does not override the equipment prohibition.

questions.explanation: General-purpose or specially attached non-mammography systems shall not be used for mammography.

variants.simpler: No bolting a paddle onto a general room.
variants.example: Accreditation will not save a prohibited configuration.

choices.text: Image receptor
choices.rationale: The receptor is beyond the breast.

choices.text: Beam-limiting device

choices.text: Acquisition workstation
choices.rationale: Displays are not in the beam path.

choices.text: PACS archive
choices.rationale: Storage is not in the beam path.

questions.explanation: Order: tube housing → beam-limiting device → paddle → breast → support/receptor.

variants.simpler: Shape the beam before it hits the patient.
variants.example: Collimation problems point to the beam-limiting device.

questions.stem: Which component produces the x-rays in a mammography unit?

choices.text: Beam-limiting device
choices.rationale: It shapes the field.

choices.text: Compression paddle
choices.rationale: It compresses tissue.

choices.text: Tube housing assembly
choices.rationale: Correct. X-rays are produced in the tube within the housing.

choices.text: Image receptor
choices.rationale: It detects remnant radiation.

variants.simpler: X-rays start in the tube housing.
variants.example: No exposure? Think generator/control/tube first.

questions.stem: Bremsstrahlung x-rays are produced when:

choices.text: An outer-shell electron falls without a vacancy being created
choices.rationale: Characteristic emission needs a vacancy.

choices.text: Electrons decelerate in the anode
choices.rationale: Correct. Bremsstrahlung means braking radiation.

choices.text: Photons scatter from the paddle toward the receptor
choices.rationale: That is not anode production.

choices.text: The grid absorbs scatter after the breast
choices.rationale: Grid action is after production.

questions.explanation: OpenStax: deceleration of electrons in the anode produces bremsstrahlung.

variants.simpler: Braking radiation = electrons slowing in the anode.
variants.example: The continuous spectrum under characteristic peaks is bremsstrahlung.

questions.stem: Why does breast imaging favor lower-energy x-ray photons than many other radiographic exams?

choices.text: Lower-energy photons penetrate thick bone better.
choices.rationale: Reversed. Lower-energy photons are attenuated more by thick material.

choices.text: Breast soft tissues absorb x-rays similarly, and lower-energy photons provide better contrast between materials.
choices.rationale: Correct. OpenStax pairs the soft-tissue contrast challenge with the higher contrast of lower-energy photons.

choices.text: Lower-energy photons eliminate the need for compression.
choices.rationale: Unsupported. Compression has its own purpose.

choices.text: Lower-energy photons produce no scatter at all.
choices.rationale: No source here supports zero scatter.

questions.explanation: OpenStax explains that lower-energy x-rays give better contrast but are attenuated more by thicker material, and that soft tissues with similar absorption are hard to separate. Breast imaging is a soft-tissue contrast problem. Device-specific kVp ranges are not given here.

variants.simpler: Breast tissues look alike to x-rays. Lower energy shows the differences better.
variants.example: This is why a thicker breast creates a trade-off between penetration and contrast.

questions.stem: A tube operates at 28 kV. Which statement about the emitted photons is correct?

choices.text: Every photon has exactly 28 keV.
choices.rationale: Bremsstrahlung produces a range of energies. The kV sets the maximum.

choices.text: Some photons exceed 28 keV because characteristic x-rays add energy.
choices.rationale: No photon can exceed the electron kinetic energy set by the accelerating voltage.

choices.text: No photon can exceed 28 keV, and photons span a range of energies below that maximum.
choices.rationale: Correct. E_max = qeV sets the ceiling, and bremsstrahlung is continuous below it.

choices.text: Photon energy depends only on mAs.
choices.rationale: mAs relates to quantity. The tube voltage sets the maximum energy.

questions.explanation: OpenStax: the maximum photon energy equals the electron kinetic energy set by the voltage (E_max = qeV, so 28 kV gives at most 28 keV). Bremsstrahlung from decelerating electrons yields a range of energies, and characteristic x-rays occur at specific energies set by the anode atoms.

variants.simpler: The kV sets the top energy. Most photons are below it.
variants.example: At 30 kV the ceiling is 30 keV, with a spread of energies below it.

questions.stem: A unit has a 65 cm source-to-image distance (SID). Under MQSA, by at most how much may the x-ray field extend beyond a side edge of the image receptor?

choices.rationale: This is 1% of SID, the limit for the paddle's chest-wall edge extending beyond the receptor's chest-wall edge.

choices.text: 1.3 cm

choices.text: 2.0 cm
choices.rationale: This treats 2% as a fixed 2 cm.

questions.explanation: MQSA lets the x-ray field extend to the chest-wall edge of the receptor but not beyond any edge by more than 2% of SID: 0.02 x 65 cm = 1.3 cm. Separately, the paddle's chest-wall edge may not extend beyond the receptor's chest-wall edge by more than 1% of SID.

variants.simpler: Take 2% of the SID: 65 x 0.02 = 1.3 cm.
variants.example: At a 70 cm SID, the same rule allows 1.4 cm.

questions.stem: During compression testing, a unit's initial power drive reaches a maximum of 230 N (about 52 lb). What is the correct conclusion?

choices.text: Compliant, because higher force always improves the image.
choices.rationale: Not a regulatory standard, and it ignores the maximum.

choices.text: It exceeds the 200 N maximum for the initial power drive. The problem must be corrected before any further exams that use the device.

variants.example: A drive that tops out at 100 N fails in the other direction because it is below 111 N.

questions.stem: A draft report lists the patient name and date of birth, exam date, facility name and location with telephone number, overall assessment category, breast density category, and recommendations to the provider. Which required element is missing?

choices.text: Technologist identification.
choices.rationale: Required on images, not in the report.

choices.text: The interpreting physician's name.
choices.rationale: Correct. MQSA requires the interpreting physician's name in the report.

choices.text: kVp and mAs.
choices.rationale: Technique values are displayed by the system, not required report contents.

choices.text: Mammography unit identification.
choices.rationale: An image-labeling item for multi-unit facilities.

questions.explanation: MQSA report contents: patient name and an additional identifier; exam date; facility name and location (city, State, ZIP, telephone); interpreting physician name; overall final assessment category; overall breast density category; and recommendations to the healthcare provider.

variants.simpler: Report items and image-label items are different lists. The reader's name belongs in the report.
variants.example: A report missing the density category would also be incomplete.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT an MQSA final assessment category?

choices.text: Probably Benign
choices.rationale: This is an MQSA final assessment category.

choices.text: Post-Procedure Mammogram for Marker Placement
choices.rationale: This is an MQSA final assessment category.

choices.text: Indeterminate: Clinical Correlation Recommended
choices.rationale: Correct. This is not one of the MQSA categories.

choices.text: Known Biopsy-Proven Malignancy
choices.rationale: This is an MQSA final assessment category.

questions.explanation: MQSA final assessment categories are Negative; Benign; Probably Benign; Suspicious; Highly Suggestive of Malignancy; Known Biopsy-Proven Malignancy; and Post-Procedure Mammogram for Marker Placement. Incomplete categories are listed separately.

variants.simpler: Seven final categories. "Indeterminate" isn't one.
variants.example: "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation" is a recognized incomplete category, not a final one.

questions.stem: In an audit period a facility performed 3,000 screening mammograms and 600 diagnostic mammograms. 270 screening exams were assessed "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation." What is the recall rate?

choices.rationale: This divides by all 3,600 exams. The recall rate uses screening exams only.
This divides 270 by the diagnostic exams.
A decimal-place error.

questions.explanation: MQSA defines the recall rate as the percentage of screening mammograms assessed "Incomplete: Need additional imaging evaluation." 270 / 3,000 = 0.09 = 9%. Diagnostic exams are not in the denominator.

variants.simpler: Recalled screening exams divided by all screening exams.
variants.example: 150 recalls among 2,000 screens is 7.5%.

questions.stem: Which statement matches MQSA's medical outcomes audit process?

choices.text: Analyses are done only when FDA requests them.
choices.rationale: MQSA sets a recurring minimum frequency.

choices.text: Analyses are done at least once every 12 months, and a designated audit interpreting physician reviews the data and notifies other interpreting physicians of their individual and facility results.
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches 21 CFR 900.12(f)(2)-(3).

choices.text: Analyses are done every 3 years with the clinical image review.
choices.rationale: Clinical image review runs on a separate 3-year cycle.

choices.text: The technologist performs the analysis and keeps the results private.
choices.rationale: MQSA designates an audit interpreting physician, and results are shared with interpreting physicians.

questions.explanation: MQSA requires audit analyses at least once every 12 months. At least one designated audit interpreting physician reviews the data, documents the results, and notifies other interpreting physicians of their individual and facility results.

variants.simpler: Yearly audit, reviewed by a designated audit physician who shares the results.
variants.example: A facility that last analyzed its audit 14 months ago is overdue.

questions.stem: Under MQSA definitions, which entity can certify a mammography facility (as opposed to accrediting it)?

choices.text: FDA, or a State that FDA has approved as a certification agency.
choices.rationale: Correct. Certification is approval by FDA or a certification agency.

choices.text: The accreditation body.
choices.rationale: The accreditation body accredits. Certification is a separate approval.

choices.text: The equipment manufacturer.
choices.rationale: Manufacturers have no certification role.

choices.text: The ARRT.
choices.rationale: ARRT credentials individuals; it does not certify facilities under MQSA.

questions.explanation: MQSA: an accreditation body is an FDA-approved entity that accredits facilities. Certification is approval of a facility to provide mammography by FDA or a certification agency (an FDA-approved State). Accreditation is a prerequisite for certification.

variants.simpler: Accreditors accredit. FDA or an approved State certifies.
variants.example: In a certification-agency State, the State, not the accreditation body, issues the certificate.

questions.stem: A facility has three mammography units. For accreditation clinical image review, what does it submit?

choices.text: One CC view from any unit.
choices.rationale: Too little. The submission is per unit and includes both views.

choices.text: Every exam from the past year.
choices.rationale: The review uses a defined sample, not every exam.

choices.text: Phantom images only.
choices.rationale: Clinical image review uses clinical images.

choices.text: CC and MLO views from two examinations for each unit.
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches 21 CFR 900.4(c)(4)(i).

questions.explanation: The accreditation body reviews clinical images from each facility at least once every 3 years. For each unit, the facility submits CC and MLO views from two examinations. Images are judged on eight attributes.

variants.simpler: Per unit: two exams, CC and MLO.
variants.example: A single-unit facility submits CC and MLO views from two exams on that unit.

questions.stem: After EQUIP's initial non-citation year, a facility receives a second, repeat Level 2 citation for its clinical image quality review requirements. According to FDA's EQUIP FAQ, what follows?

choices.text: Nothing beyond a 30-day written response, as before.
choices.rationale: This describes the first Level 2 citation. A repeat citation shortens the response time and adds a referral.

choices.text: Immediate permanent certificate revocation.
choices.rationale: Not the described EQUIP pathway.

choices.text: A written response within 15 days and referral to the accreditation body for clinical image evaluation.
choices.rationale: Correct. This matches FDA's compliance pathway for a repeat Level 2.

choices.text: The technologist's personal ARRT credential is suspended.
choices.rationale: EQUIP citations are facility compliance actions.

questions.explanation: FDA's EQUIP FAQ: after the initial non-citation year, clinical image quality review deficiencies are cited as Level 2 with a written response due within 30 days. A repeat Level 2 requires a response within 15 days and referral to the accreditation body for clinical image evaluation.

variants.simpler: Repeat Level 2: 15-day response plus an accreditation body image check.
variants.example: A first-time deficiency still gets the 30-day response.
